scope: The cookbook's `triggers` field (the activity tags a guideline carries so an agent loads only the guidelines relevant to what it is doing now), the controlled vocabulary of trigger values, how a guideline chooses its triggers, how the vocabulary is governed (added to, renamed, retired, with the artifacts migrated), the trigger index an agent queries, the checkpoint pattern of loading (always, on activity, pre-commit, pre-PR), and how the cookbook checks that trigger-filtered loading picks the guidelines a task needs. Out of scope: RFC 2119 keyword case and severity (sibling topic requirement-keywords) and general just-in-time context loading (context-and-memory-management: should-retrieve-context-just-in-time, must-not-front-load-context), which this record cites but does not restate.
research_type: Technology / software (intent: Decide; domain: retrieval and agent context selection, controlled vocabularies). Technical MEDIUM bar for host and tool documentation; Statistical bar for every metric claim (precision, recall, accuracy, token figures, evidence that filtering helps or harms).

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient, go to authoritative sources (the agent hosts' own documentation from Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and GitHub; the W3C SKOS Recommendation and Primer; NISO's ISO 25964 description and ANSI/NISO Z39.19; peer-reviewed or preprint evaluations for metric claims), chain citations, corroborate across independent publishers, record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch per research question (conditional instruction loading in each agent host; metadata filtering in retrieval APIs; controlled-vocabulary construction, maintenance and evaluation; long-context and instruction-density evaluations; tool-selection retrieval; tag governance on a large tagging site; staged checks in commit and CI tooling). Every cited page was fetched with WebFetch or curl (GitHub Docs via their article-body Markdown endpoint; arXiv abstracts and PDFs; the Z39.19 and IIR chapter 8 PDFs converted to text) and every quote copied from the fetched text.
methodology.inclusion: Primary: agent-host documentation (Claude Code memory and skills, Agent Skills, tool search; Cursor rules; GitHub Copilot custom instructions; AGENTS.md and Codex; OpenAI file search), retrieval-API docs (Pinecone), vocabulary standards (W3C SKOS Reference and Primer, NISO ISO 25964 page, ANSI/NISO Z39.19), git and pre-commit docs, GitHub branch-protection docs, the IIR textbook chapter on evaluation, arXiv/TACL studies. Secondary only where no primary covers the point (martinfowler.com on staged builds; Stack Overflow's help center for a per-item tag cap and tag governance as practised on a large site), flagged in each trust basis.
methodology.exclusion: Search-result snippets; pages that could not be fetched (nlp.stanford.edu's IIR site refused connections, so a university-hosted copy of chapter 8 was used); the ISO 25964 text itself (paywalled); blogs, SEO articles and vendor marketing; any claim without a fetched verbatim quote.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy/verifiability 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, capped by the domain bar (Technical MEDIUM; Statistical MED-HIGH for metric claims, where an undisclosed sample or an unrefereed study scores low); secondary sources scored at most 72; prior cookbook text scored 0.

summary: The design holds: every agent host now loads instructions conditionally (Claude Code path-scoped rules and skills, Cursor rule types, Copilot applyTo, metadata filters in OpenAI file search and Pinecone), and the evaluations that exist (Lost in the Middle, IFScale, Chroma's context-rot report, RAG-MCP) show that more context and more instructions degrade model performance, which is the direction the trigger guide assumes. A small closed vocabulary with scope notes and examples is what Z39.19 and SKOS prescribe, and outside practice supports a union query, frontmatter declaration, a per-item tag cap of 5, and nominating a new term before use. Every rule that carries a number (240, 10-20, ~12, 27, ~10) is unsupported: no source measures tag-filtered guideline loading for coding agents, and no source supports those counts. The 'most effective' claim for graduated checkpoints and the proportional-cost rule have no study behind them. The index location, regeneration command, generated-not-hand-edited rule, ordering, guideline-only scope and empty-list default are internal choices no outside source addresses. Research adds governance (scope notes, history notes, renames with the old value kept as an alias, retirement with impact assessment and migration, periodic review of overused and unused values), mechanical validation of trigger values, a fallback for tag misses, and evaluation with a labelled task set reporting recall and precision.
open_questions: Whether `refactor` (17 guidelines) and `research` (10 guidelines), in use at the base commit but absent from the canonical table, are nominated and added to the table or migrated to existing values; the governance verdicts give the procedure, not the outcome.

Whether the guide keeps any counts (240 guidelines, 10-20 per query, ~12 for writing-tests, 27 principles, ~10 pre-commit rules): no source supports them and the cookbook's own state has outgrown them, so the owner decides between generated counts, ranges measured by an evaluation, or no numbers.

Whether the pre-commit set stays 'mandatory' when git lets every pre-commit hook be bypassed with --no-verify, or whether the mandatory gate moves to a check the agent cannot skip (a required status check on the pull request).

Whether trigger-filtered loading gets a fallback (a description- or keyword-based search over all guidelines, as Cursor's Apply Intelligently, Claude Code skill descriptions and the tool search tool do) for tasks whose tags miss a guideline, and how far the cookbook trades precision for recall there.

What size of labelled task set the cookbook adopts to measure trigger selection: IIR's rule of thumb is 50 information needs, skill-creator uses 20 queries split 60/40; the owner sets the number and the recall target.

Whether the 1-5 cap stays as is: Stack Overflow caps a question at 5 tags, while at the base commit no guideline carries more than 4 triggers; the owner decides whether the cap is 5, 4 or a soft warning.
limitations: No peer-reviewed or preprint study was found that measures tag- or trigger-filtered loading of coding guidelines for an agent; the metric claims rest on proxies (multi-document question answering, needle and distractor tasks, keyword-inclusion instruction density, tool selection over MCP registries).

Anthropic's tool-search accuracy figures (49% to 74%, 79.5% to 88.1%) and its 85% token reduction come from internal testing with no disclosed sample, so they fail the Statistical bar and are scored low.
RAG-MCP (arXiv:2505.03275) and IFScale (arXiv:2507.11538) are unrefereed preprints; Chroma's context-rot report is a vendor technical report.
The text of ISO 25964 is paywalled; only NISO's public description of the standard was fetched. Z39.19 (2005, reaffirmed 2010) was used for the detailed construction and maintenance rules.
nlp.stanford.edu, the publisher-hosted copy of Introduction to Information Retrieval, refused connections; chapter 8 was read from a university course archive copy of the same chapter.

No outside source addresses the internal design rules on the index's file location, the `cookr update` regeneration command, a generated index never being hand-edited, ordering triggers from specific to general, the field being guideline-only, or an empty list meaning not yet classified.
The only source found for a numeric per-item tag cap is Stack Overflow's help center (5 tags per question), a single site's policy rather than a standard.
Apple, Android and Windows have no bearing on this topic and were not researched; the platforms here are the agent hosts and the vocabulary standards.
Inter-indexer consistency evidence comes from one small study (three articles, student and professional indexers); it shows tagging is inconsistent but does not measure trigger assignment.
